description: Research-quality eval cases. Durable, verifiable answers so grading is stable across runs; each benefits from web research. key_points are facts a complete answer must contain (drives Key-Point-Recall); answer is the reference for the SimpleQA-style CORRECT/INCORRECT/NOT_ATTEMPTED judge.

cases.question: Who are the authors of the book 'The Pragmatic Programmer', and in what year was the first edition published?
cases.answer: Andrew Hunt and David Thomas; the first edition was published in 1999.

cases.question: What does HTTP status code 429 mean, and what response header commonly accompanies it to tell the client when to retry?
cases.answer: 429 means 'Too Many Requests' (the client is being rate-limited); the Retry-After header commonly indicates when to retry.

cases.question: Which organization originally sponsored the development of the Rust programming language, and in what year was Rust 1.0 released?
cases.answer: Mozilla originally sponsored Rust; Rust 1.0 was released in 2015.

cases.question: Approximately how many unique addresses does IPv4 provide, and why is that the limit?
cases.answer: About 4.3 billion addresses, because IPv4 uses 32-bit addresses (2^32 ≈ 4.29 billion).

cases.question: Who developed the general theory of relativity, and in what year was it published?
cases.answer: Albert Einstein developed general relativity; it was published in 1915.

cases.question: In Semantic Versioning (SemVer), what do the three numbers in MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH each signify, and when must the MAJOR version be incremented?
cases.answer: MAJOR for incompatible API changes, MINOR for backward-compatible added functionality, PATCH for backward-compatible bug fixes; MAJOR must be incremented when you make incompatible (breaking) API changes.
